name: Federated States of Micronesia
prevalence_note: On 1 June 2026 the Office of the President warned that some social-media accounts and online posts were falsely claiming a link to the President, and that misleading and possibly AI-generated material was circulating, including altered images, distorted official seals or logos, fabricated announcements, and scam-related posts with inaccurate information and obvious language errors. Much earlier, on 20 August 2010, the Banking Board, the Financial Intelligence Unit of the National Police and the Department of Justice publicly described a rise in email crime aimed at the FSM, typically promising large incoming transfers and asking for personal and account information.
cross_border_note: The 2010 government notice suggested the rise might be linked to more wire-transfer offices opening in the FSM, and the example it quoted was framed as money waiting at an international transfer counter. Official national announcements are said to appear on the official Office of the President Facebook page and on the government website. A +691 number is not proof that a message comes from a Palikir office.

scams.name: Fake presidential or government social-media posts, including scam-related material
scams.name_en: Office of the President, June 2026: unofficial pages and possibly AI-generated posts misuse seals or logos, invent announcements, and include scam-related content that is not an official channel
context_keywords: scam post that claims a Palikir office sent it

red_flag_keywords.text: this page is the Office of the President, send your details
official seal on a post that asks for money or data
fabricated government announcement in your feed
follow this unofficial account for Palikir updates

scams.signals_en: The FSM Office of the President warned of unauthorised social pages and potentially AI-generated posts using distorted seals, fake announcements and grammar errors for scams, urging reliance only on the official Facebook page and gov site.
scams.legit_en: Official announcements and press updates from the FSM Office of the President appear only on its verified Facebook page and the official government website. A page using a seal in a scam post is not official.
bait_tactics: Do not treat a social-media page as official merely because it uses a presidential or national seal, and check the claim against the government's published site or the official Facebook page named in the announcement.
Refuse any request in such a post for personal or banking information, or for a payment.
Avoid spreading the post on until it has been checked against those official channels.

scams.name: Unsolicited email promising a large transfer and asking for account data
scams.name_en: August 2010 Banking Board, National Police FIU and Department of Justice warning: a rise in email crime targeting the FSM, including messages that promise large incoming transfers and then ask for name, address, telephone and account numbers
context_keywords: unsolicited email promising money in the FSM
collect a transfer at a wire office
request for account and telephone numbers
email asking you to cash a cheque

red_flag_keywords.text: a large sum is already waiting if you send your details
reply with your name, address, phone and account number
cash this cheque and pass the money on
unsolicited mail asking for a charitable donation

scams.signals_en: An Aug 2010 FSM notice (Banking Board, Police FIU, DOJ) warned of email scams promising money to steal personal/bank data, flagging spam links, unknown senders, requests for account details, cheques to cash, or fake charity appeals.
scams.legit_en: A real transfer or official payment in the FSM never requires replying to an unexpected email with account/ID details or cashing a stranger's cheque. As the government noted, unsolicited windfalls too good to be true are scams.
bait_tactics: Do not reply with identity or account details, and do not cash a cheque or collect a transfer just because an unexpected email promised a large sum.
Ignore links in unsolicited mail, and check any real payment only through the customer's own bank or a known transfer office.
If money or data may already have been exposed, raise it with the bank and with the National Police, as that 2010 notice advised.
